We want to open-source our internal CLI. What do we do before and after we flip it public?
expected_behavior: runs or asks for a full-history secret scan before anything else, not just the current tree
checks for client names, internal ticket keys and personal data, and stops to ask the owner if anything is questionable
recommends settling the repo name before the repo goes public
orders the launch as repo, canonical write-up, community posts, then wider channels
labels advice as verified, observed or general rather than stating all of it as fact

cases.prompt: Audit github.com/acme/widget-cli for search visibility
expected_behavior: runs scripts/check_repo_seo.py rather than guessing at the repo state
tells the owner the social preview image must be uploaded manually in Settings
does not add inaccurate topics or keyword-stuff the description

cases.prompt: Publish my MCP server to all the registries
expected_behavior: completes the plain repo checklist first, then the registry steps
starts with the Official MCP Registry using server.json and mcp-publisher, since other registries ingest from it
prepares one set of submission copy and reuses it for every listing
flags that manual registries have review queues and should not be resubmitted

cases.prompt: My MCP server ships only as a Docker image. How do I publish it to the official registry?
expected_behavior: uses registryType oci with an identifier of the form registry/namespace/repository:tag
adds the io.modelcontextprotocol.server.name label to the image and matches it to the server.json name
fills websiteUrl and keeps the description at 100 characters or fewer
tells the owner that mcp-publisher login is interactive and theirs to run
labels registry facts with a verification date rather than stating them from memory
